limits: THE SECOND REGISTRATION FOR THIS GATE, and it covers the lane the sibling one cannot. `controls/flow-finish-gate` forces the Makefile fallback because a fixture cannot supply a CPP checkout with a working lib.cicd; this one stubs `uv` instead, so the gate takes its PRIMARY path and the subject is what it does with the runner's JSON. WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that a quality gate the runner DECLARED and then never ran - absent from `step_details` and absent from `skipped` - makes the gate FAIL. Fail rather than warn, on the wave orchestrator's ruling and for a reason worth keeping: #628's `warn (skipped gates: X)` means the gate could not run AND records why, which is a consistent runner reporting a repository fact. This has no reason - the runner declared the gate and both of its own records of what became of it omit it - so the accounting itself is inconsistent, and a green from that is the false green the whole chain exists to stop. WHAT IT DOES NOT: anything about whether the runner was right to drop it, or about the Makefile fallback, or about `make verify` itself. THE BAD CASE IS A FIELD ARTIFACT, NOT A CONSTRUCTION. `cases/bad-declared-never-ran/runner.json` is the verbatim JSON from the run that produced this issue's own regression on 2026-09-20: the finish plan declared five gates, `.claude/cicd_tasks.yml` listed four, `get_plan_steps` prefers the manifest over BUILTIN_PLANS, and the gate printed `ok` over a run that never executed `verify` while its own `gates` array named it. It was caught by a WALL-CLOCK figure - 163.68s, unchanged after a 229.8s step was supposedly added - and not by any instrument, which is the argument for this control existing at all. The GOOD case is the same artifact with `verify` accounted for in `step_details`, so an anchor that simply always passed, or a gate that warned on every run, fails here. THE STUB IS `uv`, NOT A REAL RUNNER: the gate reads the runner's JSON off STDOUT through `tee`, so a case that wrote a file somewhere would be testing nothing (the #812 rule this repository already records). `cp` of the case dir is not enough either - the gate needs a directory containing CLAUDE.md to accept as the CPP checkout, which each case supplies as `cpp/`.

anchors.why: The gate exactly as it stood at af348f8, vendored byte-for-byte, the same article the sibling control uses. Vendored twice rather than shared across the two control directories on purpose: the tracking check enumerates files UNDER each control directory, so a path reaching out of it would be untracked from that control's point of view - and a control whose anchor is not in the repository behaves correctly here and has no anchor at all in a clean clone (#978). It MISSES the known-bad input in the most direct way available: handed the byte-identical JSON from the field run, it prints `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: ok` and exits 0. It cannot do otherwise - it has no notion of a declared gate set, since the set it filters against is a literal in its own source. It agrees with the fixed gate on the known-good case.
